summary: Iteration 32 — production-readiness regression pass (backend only). Added /app/backend/tests/test_iter32_regression.py with 24 test cases spanning AUTH/RBAC, idempotency, ledger invariants, refund flow, reversal, outbound/inbound webhooks, demo UPI checkout, reconciliation export (method column + breakdown), refunds provider_key, reports CSV method column, and currency catalog. All 24/24 PASS against the public preview URL.
critical_code_review_comments: PRODUCTION GAP (as flagged in the request, REPORT-ONLY): app/routers/config.py provider_inbound_webhook (lines 260-311) reconciles a payment to a normalized status via the state machine but INTENTIONALLY does NOT post a ledger credit and does NOT compute fee/net when transitioning pending -> succeeded. For MOCK and DEMO_UPI (synchronous providers) the charge flow has already posted the credit, so this is safe today. For a FUTURE real async provider (e.g., a live UPI/PSP that returns pending on create and confirms via webhook), a webhook-driven pending -> succeeded transition would leave fee_minor/net_minor NULL AND ledger un-credited — a silent money-loss defect. Recommendation: in provider_inbound_webhook, when transitioning from a non-terminal state INTO a success state, call fee_engine.compute_fee + ledger_service.post_entry ONLY if no existing payment credit exists yet (mirror the guard already used in capture_payment via _existing_payment_credit). This preserves idempotency and closes the gap without breaking synchronous providers.

config.py: The inbound-webhook idempotency check compares prev == event.normalized_status BEFORE the state-machine `can_transition` guard. Fine functionally, but adds a subtle behaviour: a duplicate webhook with the SAME final status returns {already: <status>}, while a webhook that transitions from an invalid source returns {skipped: true}. Consider also returning 200 for BOTH (currently both are 200) but including provider_txn_id so operators can correlate — small DX win.

payments.py list_refunds: uses a Row-level tuple + zip via `res.all()`; correctly avoids N+1 by joining Payment once. Consider replacing the ad-hoc RefundOut.model_validate + attribute assignment with an ORM relationship or subquery, but current impl is fine for a 200-row page.

checkout.py public_demo_upi_pay: idempotency_key is f'demoupi_{token}' — safe (unique per session). Good. However, when outcome != 'success' the endpoint does not persist the simulated attempt anywhere; operators cannot audit the walkthrough. Consider dropping an audit-log row for the failed/pending simulation for support-team traceability.

reconciliation.py _pm_from_payment: falls back to 'card' when metadata.method is absent and provider_key != 'demo_upi'. If a NEW UPI provider is introduced (razorpay-upi, cashfree-upi), reconciliation will misclassify UPI rails as card. Recommend centralising method inference — either via a persisted Payment.payment_method column (already accepted at create-time, just not persisted on the OUT schema/reconciliation join) or a provider-plugin capability declaration.
